findings.title: With several override ranges on one day, every slot outside the first range is rejected.
findings.body: `dateOverrides.find` returns true as soon as one override on the slot's date doesn't contain the slot. Take a day with overrides 09:00–10:00 and 14:00–15:00: a 14:00 slot is after the end of the first range, so `find` matches and the slot is rejected even though the second range covers it. The fix is to collect the overrides for that date and reject the slot only if no range contains it.

held.title: `override.timeZone` is optional, and when it is missing the server's default timezone is used.
held.body: `TimeRange.timeZone` is optional and only `getSchedule` fills it in. Any other caller of `getTimeSlots` that passes overrides without `timeZone` ends up calling `.tz(undefined)`, which uses the default or server timezone. The computed offset is then wrong unless the server runs in the organizer's timezone. I could not check the other callers from here. Fall back to `organizerTimeZone` when `override.timeZone` is unset.
